material_systems.name: Standard Wood Primer for Railing Components

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start High-Hiding Primer
primer.notes: Standard primer for bare wood railing components (balusters, newels, handrails, base rails). For hardwood species prone to tannin bleed, substitute SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK. For poplar, substitute SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. General-purpose wood primer for standard softwood/composite railing components.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood railing components (oak, cherry, walnut newels/handrails). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood substrates.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare poplar railing components. Green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for poplar.

material_systems.name: DTM Acrylic Primer for Bare Iron

products: Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial DTM Acrylic Primer/Finish
Benjamin Moore IronClad DTM Acrylic Enamel
primer.notes: For bare iron/steel balusters. SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning MANDATORY before priming — oils and drawing compounds from manufacturing cause fish-eye defects and delamination. Do NOT use standard wood primer on iron. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.4.

material_systems.notes: Applies only to iron balusters when railing_type=iron_and_wood. Solvent cleaning is prerequisite.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Powder-Coated Iron

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start All Purpose Primer
primer.notes: For iron balusters with factory powder coat. Scuff-sand with 180-220 grit BEFORE priming. Self-etching primers do NOT work on powder coat — must use bonding primer. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.4.

material_systems.notes: Applies only to powder-coated iron balusters. Self-etching = WRONG PRODUCT.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Good for enclosed stairwells where yellowing is a concern. Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away. Sands easily between coats. Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush/roll typically requires 3+ coats per FFD 15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Polyurethane Topcoat for Handrails

products: General Finishes High Performance Water Based Topcoat
topcoat.notes: Optional QT5 upgrade — additional clear coat over enamel finish on handrails ONLY. Provides hand-oil resistance. Water-based poly to avoid yellowing over white/light colors. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.1.

material_systems.notes: Optional. Handrails only. QT5 only. Additional clear coat for hand-oil resistance.

coverage_profiles.notes: Railing primer coverage for EA items (balusters, newels). Baluster SF per unit: square ≈ 1.5-2.0 SF, turned ≈ 2.0-3.0 SF. Newel SF per unit: ≈ 4-8 SF depending on size and ornament. Iron balusters (DTM primer) may have slightly lower coverage due to slick surface.
assumptions: Baluster SF varies by profile (square < turned)

coverage_profiles.notes: Railing primer coverage for LF items (handrails, base rails). Handrail: 4 paintable sides (top, 2 sides, underside) ≈ 1.5-2.0 SF per LF. Base rail: 3 sides ≈ 0.75-1.0 SF per LF.

Railing finish coverage for EA items on primed smooth surface. Spray method: add 20-30% material waste for overspray on complex profiles. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage.
assumptions: Baluster SF per unit varies by profile

coverage_profiles.notes: Railing finish coverage for LF items on primed smooth surface. Handrail has 4 paintable surfaces — use 1.75 SF per LF for material quantity. Base rail has 3 surfaces — use 0.875 SF per LF.

consumables.name: Ram Board Stair Armor tread protector
consumables.usage: Mandatory tread protection throughout all railing work
consumables.notes: Per tread. If already installed from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC, verify integrity rather than replace. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads — extreme fall hazard.

consumables.name: Low-tack safe-release masking tape
consumables.usage: Secure tread protection without damaging tread finish
consumables.notes: Low-tack prevents tread finish damage during protection removal.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Initial bare wood sanding, factory primer scuff on wood components
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial sanding of bare wood balusters/newels/handrails.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Final prep sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces (FFD 15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required.

consumables.name: Scotch-Brite abrasive pad (180-220 grit equivalent)
consumables.usage: Scuff-sand powder-coated iron balusters before bonding primer
consumables.notes: Conformable pad follows baluster profile better than flat sandpaper. 180-220 grit equivalent for powder coat scuff.

consumables.name: Solvent cleaner for SSPC-SP 1 metal prep
consumables.usage: Mandatory solvent cleaning of all iron/steel balusters before any primer
consumables.notes: SSPC-SP 1 solvent wipe. Removes manufacturing oils and drawing compounds. Non-negotiable first step for all iron balusters. One quart covers ~100 balusters.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for handrail, newel, and base rail surfaces
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat and slightly profiled surfaces. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5")
consumables.usage: Detail work for baluster profiles and junction cut-in
consumables.notes: 1.5-inch for baluster detail. Particularly useful for square balusters and junction work.

consumables.name: German round trim brush 1.25 inch
consumables.usage: Purpose-made for turned/ornate baluster complex profiles
consumables.notes: Round profile follows turned baluster contours. Significantly reduces roping on complex profiles. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 12.1.

consumables.name: Flow additive (Floetrol/Penetrol)
consumables.usage: Extends working time, improves leveling on detail-intensive baluster work
consumables.notes: Floetrol for latex, Penetrol for alkyd. Prevents roping on complex profiles. One quart conditions approximately 4 quarts of finish. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.4.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 or HVLP nozzle
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for baluster/railing spray finish
consumables.notes: HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work (less overspray). If airless: fine-finish tips (Graco FFLP 108, 210/310 series, 4-6 inch fan). Per doctrine 6.3.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~20 balusters or ~20 LF handrail. Use before every coat.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking for spray containment, baluster junction taping (when taping technique used)
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall masking for spray. Also for baluster-to-handrail junction taping (~1 ft per baluster × 2 sides).

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.notes: Runner-style for landings. Required when floor_type = finished or partial.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Caulk at newel-to-tread and newel-to-handrail junctions
consumables.notes: Newel junction caulk — fills visible gaps at newel base and newel-to-handrail connection. One tube covers approximately 25 LF of caulk joint.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes, minor defects on wood railing components
consumables.notes: Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding on flat surfaces. Mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. For handrail flat surfaces and newel flat panels.

stair_tread_covers.description: Mandatory tread protection throughout all railing work
stair_tread_covers.condition: ALWAYS — mandatory regardless of method. May already be in place from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at landing areas

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking for overspray containment when spraying balusters

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: Iron DTM primer applies ONLY when railing_type=iron_and_wood AND substrate_state=SS_BARE
compatibility_rules.result: SYS_PRIMER_IRON_DTM on iron balusters, wood primers on wood components
compatibility_rules.notes: Mixed system — iron balusters get DTM primer, wood newels/handrails get standard wood primer. Both applied in prime module.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer on powder coat — NOT self-etching
compatibility_rules.notes: Self-etching primers do NOT work on powder coat. Scuff-sand 180-220 grit then bonding primer. Per doctrine 4.4.

compatibility_rules.description: Polyurethane topcoat compatible with all enamel finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based poly over cured enamel. Allow full cure of enamel before poly application.

risk_notes.risk: Manufacturing oils and drawing compounds cause fish-eye defects and primer delamination on iron balusters
risk_notes.mitigation: SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning is MANDATORY first step for ALL iron/steel balusters before any primer.

risk_notes.risk: Self-etching primer fails on powder-coated iron — causes delamination
risk_notes.mitigation: Scuff-sand 180-220 grit + bonding primer ONLY (SYS_PRIMER_POWDER_COAT_BOND). Never self-etching.

risk_notes.topic: Tread damage from drips during railing work
risk_notes.risk: Drips from overhead baluster/handrail painting damage unprotected treads
risk_notes.mitigation: Tread protection mandatory from Day 1. Ram Board Stair Armor — never plastic sheeting (fall hazard).

risk_notes.risk: Fast-drying waterborne product creates visible brush marks (roping) on complex turned profiles
risk_notes.mitigation: Use flow additive (CON_FLOW_ADDITIVE). German round trim brushes for turned profiles. Thin coats.

risk_notes.risk: Excessive film build on handrail underside causes runs and sags
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats, proper flow additive. QT4+ remove brackets and paint handrails horizontally.

risk_notes.risk: Green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare poplar.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths (3 wood primers + 2 iron primers). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven. Any primer can pair with any finish. Optional poly topcoat at QT5 for handrails.
material_notes.iron_wood_mixed_primer: When railing_type=iron_and_wood, iron balusters receive DTM or bonding primer while wood newels/handrails receive standard wood primer. Two primer types in same job — applied in same prime module.
material_notes.coverage_note: Balusters: EA × ~1.5-3.0 SF depending on profile. Newels: EA × ~4-8 SF. Handrails: LF × ~1.75 SF per LF (4-surface). Base rails: LF × ~0.875 SF per LF.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).
material_notes.flow_additive_note: Floetrol for latex, Penetrol for alkyd. Extends working time 25-50%. Critical for brush application on turned balusters.

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim/window/riser spec coverage

assumptions.value: Square ≈ 1.5-2.0 SF, Turned ≈ 2.0-3.0 SF per baluster
assumptions.source: Estimated from typical baluster dimensions (34-36 inch height, 1.25-1.75 inch profile)

assumptions.value: ≈ 1.75 SF per LF (4-surface coverage: top, 2 sides, underside)
assumptions.source: Estimated from typical handrail profile (~2.5 inch width × 3 inch height)
